props.gloss_en: 'vehayu' teaches that one may not read out of order
'these words... upon your heart' teaches that [the Shema] requires intent
the whole paragraph requires intent -- rejected as a יכול by R' Eliezer (13a.36), asserted by R' Akiva (13b.1)
the verse says 'these': to here intent is required
R' Eliezer: up to 'these' [the Shema] requires intent
from 'these' on [the Shema] requires intent -- which R' Eliezer denies
R' Akiva: 'which I command you this day, upon your heart' -- from here you learn that the whole paragraph requires intent
Rabba bar bar Chana in R' Yochanan's name: the halakha follows R' Akiva
one who reads the Shema must focus his heart
R' Acha in R' Yehuda's name: once he has focused his heart in the first paragraph, he need not [focus] again
Rabba bar bar Chana in R' Yochanan's name (as this tradition places it): the halakha follows R' Acha who said it in R' Yehuda's name
Rav Zutra: 'upon your heart' -- to here the mitzva of intent, from here on the mitzva of recitation (the utterance; its law is the stam's construal at 13b.6)
R' Yoshiya: to here the mitzva of recitation, from here on the mitzva of intent (the utterance; construed in the next piska, 13b.9-12)
this is what Rav Zutra means: to here the mitzva of intent AND recitation; from here on, recitation without intent
Rav Zutra (as construed): up to 'upon your heart', intent is required
Rav Zutra (as construed): up to 'upon your heart', recitation is required
Rav Zutra (as construed): from 'upon your heart' on, recitation is required
from 'upon your heart' on, intent is required -- which Rav Zutra (as construed) denies
R' Yitzchak: 'and you shall place these words' -- the placing [of the tefillin] must be opposite the heart

objections.gloss_en: מאי שנא מכאן ואילך מצות קריאה -- דכתיב לדבר בם? הכא נמי הא כתיב ודברת בם! -- if recitation is the mitzva only from 'upon your heart' on because 'to speak of them' is written there, the first paragraph has 'and you shall speak of them' too

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: עד כאן מצות כוונה וקריאה, מכאן ואילך קריאה בלא כוונה -- recitation runs throughout; what changes at 'upon your heart' is that intent stops (= p_rz_reading)

objections.gloss_en: ומאי שנא עד כאן מצות כוונה וקריאה דכתיב על לבבך ודברת בם? התם נמי הא כתיב על לבבכם לדבר בם! -- the second paragraph too has 'upon your heart', so intent should be required there as well

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא מבעי ליה לכדרבי יצחק -- the second paragraph's 'upon your heart' is needed for R' Yitzchak's teaching that the tefillin are placed opposite the heart (= p_sima_keneged_halev), so it does not teach intent
